purpose: Show that the strict V6 SSE guard (P7F1V6SseGuard) does not refuse streams the Alibaba route really sent, before it is used on a live run.
source: F1Q raw SSE bodies, C:/dhx-f1q branch experiment/p7-f1-semantic-question-v1, artifacts/web-pdf-semantic-diagnostic (response.sse and response.sse.gz)

guardResultOnTheSameBodies.note: The 4 error-payload streams are reported by the assembly check (STREAM_ERROR), not by the guard; the 1 data line that is not JSON is reported as STREAM_MALFORMED.

rules: event: error in any spelling of the value -> STREAM_ERROR_EVENT, even if the payload has no error key
id:, retry: or any field other than data -> STREAM_FIELD_UNKNOWN
a data event that is not an object, or has neither choices nor error -> STREAM_EVENT_SHAPE_UNKNOWN
comments (a line starting with a colon) and blank lines are allowed
limit: A survey of one route's past streams: it shows the guard does not refuse what was sent then. It does not prove the route will never add another field.
